title: unified-enriched-log-boarding-and-tenant-resiliency-shim
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight 'boarding' shim that runs at the telemetry ingress layer to normalize structured logs, enforce correlation ID lifecycle (generation/TTL/preservation), and provide tenant-resiliency features (per-tenant throttles, graceful degradation and bounded fanout) before handoff to downstream Kafka/Loki/ELK pipelines. The shim should be deployable at edge gateways and as a sidecar for on-prem/private deployments.
background: We continue to see two classes of production issues: 1) inconsistent correlation ID propagation across language-specific loggers causing poor trace joins in dashboards, and 2) bursty tenant traffic that overwhelms downstream aggregators (Loki/Elastic/Kafka) and causes long tail latencies or partial drops. Previous efforts focused on schema validation and enrichment in the core ingest fleet but lacked a lightweight, tenant-aware gate that can: add canonical trace_id when missing, attach correlation TTL to prevent cross-request pollution, and apply tenant-scoped backpressure or local buffering. This ticket is the boarding shim design+implementation and the canary rollout plan.
design_notes:
- Boarding shim responsibilities: parse incoming event (json/text), detect/normalize timestamp and severity, ensure canonical correlation_id (trace_id) header exists, attach correlation_ttl (default 5m), add tenant_id tag from auth token or host header, compute small deterministic shard_key and write to local in-memory reservoir if downstream overloaded.
- Resilience model: per-tenant token-bucket with burst allowance; when over limit, apply progressive degradation: 1) drop verbose fields (stack traces, payload.blobs) 2) sample events 3) return 429 with retry-after for upstream clients if configured.
- Guarantees: idempotent enrichment, ordering best-effort within shard_key, no amplification of payload size beyond 20%.
- Compatibility: output JSON line compatible with current Loki/Fluent forwarder and Kafka topic schema v3. A feature-flag controls correlation_ttl behaviour for private deployments (default on for hosted).
- Implementation: Rust binary using simd-json for fast parsing, optional WASM build for edge runtimes. Expose metrics via Prometheus endpoint on /metrics and health+ready endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Boarding shim builds and passes unit+integration tests in CI
Canary deployed to 5% of ingress nodes for 48 hours with no more than 0.1% increase in median ingest latency and <=0.5% increase in P99 latency
Trace join success increases by >=40% on canary traffic (instrumented via test trace set), measured by correlation_id presence and successful trace stitch in tracing backend
Per-tenant backpressure prevents downstream errors during synthetic burst test: downstream error rate stays <0.2%
All events emitted to downstream retain canonical fields required by dashboards (timestamp, tenant_id, trace_id, service.name, severity)
tasks: Prototype boarding shim binary (Rust) and benchmark parse/enrich throughput
Implement correlation_id generation + TTL semantics and header canonicalization
Add per-tenant token-bucket and backpressure policy with config knobs
Expose /metrics and generate Prometheus labels: ingress_rate, enrich_errors, dropped_by_policy, reservoir_depth, correlation_missing_count
Create integration test harness that replays production sample and synthetic bursts
Add feature-flag gating and config maps for private deployments
Prepare canary rollout automation and rollback criteria in deployment pipeline
Update Loki/ELK forwarder mapping and Kafka schema compatibility tests
Document operational runbook and add runbook to on-call rotation
rollout_plan: Alpha: run on 2 non-prod ingress nodes behind feature-flag for 72h and validate metrics
Beta: 5% of host ingress traffic for 48h, monitor key SLIs and trace-join success; auto-rollback on threshold breach
Canary: 25% of region traffic with increased throttling visibility and alerting enabled
GA: gradual increase to 100% with staged removals of legacy enrichers once GA is stable
monitoring: Create Loki dashboards: ingest_latency_by_node, enrich_error_stream, dropped_events_by_tenant
Add alert: dropped_events_rate > 0.5% over 5m => P0 on-call
Add alert: P99 ingest latency increase > 200ms vs baseline => investigate canary
Create trace-join success panel (percent of requests with valid trace_id and successful stitch)
test_plan: Unit tests for parsing variants (json, ndjson, plain text fallback)
Fuzz tests for malformed payloads and oversized events
Integration: replay historical 24h production sample and assert no data loss beyond controlled sampling
Chaos: simulate downstream Kafka/Loki lag and assert boarding shim applies reservoir/backpressure rules and bounded memory usage
Benchmark: sustained 10k rps node with 50% large payloads and measure CPU/memory under baseline-constrained conditions
risks: Potential increase in ingress node CPU due to parsing/enrichment—mitigate with simd-json and feature-flag CPU limits
Misclassification of tenant_id leading to wrong throttling—mitigate via conservative heuristics and telemetry to detect mismatches
Incompatible schema transformation causing dashboard regressions—mitigate with compatibility tests and mapping layer
Operational complexity across hosted/dedicated/private variants—mitigate by shipping clear config profiles and a small surface area of knobs
